transcript.text: Samsung WW90T534DAW keeps coming up with 4C after a couple of minutes. Drum is dry. Any ideas before I call someone out?

The 4C error code on Samsung washing machines (specifically the WW series) stands for "Water Supply Problem" or "Slow Water Fill." It means the machine has not filled to the required level within a specific time frame.

Since you mentioned the drum is dry, this confirms water isn't entering at all (or very slowly). Before calling a technician, try these troubleshooting steps in order:

### 1. Check the Most Common Causes
• Is the tap turned on? Ensure both hot and cold taps behind the machine are fully open.
• Has there been a recent water cut-off? If your mains water was interrupted recently, air may be trapped in the lines. Turn off the machine, turn the taps off for 30 seconds, then turn them back on and restart.

### 2. Inspect the Inlet Hoses
• Kinked hoses: Check if the inlet hose is bent or kinked behind the machine.
• Frozen pipes (if applicable): If you’re in a cold area and the hose is outside, it might be frozen.
• Low water pressure: Test the water flow by disconnecting the hose from the back of the machine and turning on the tap briefly into a bucket. If the flow is weak, the issue is with your home’s water supply, not the machine.

### 3. Clean the Inlet Valve Filters (Most Likely Fix)
This is the number one cause of 4C errors. The small mesh filters inside the inlet valves can get clogged with sand, rust, or debris over time.
• Turn off both hot and cold taps.
• Unscrew the inlet hoses from the back of the washing machine.
• Inside the hose connection point on the machine, you’ll see a small plastic/mesh filter. Remove it carefully (use pliers if needed, but be gentle).
• Clean the filter under running water with an old toothbrush to remove any debris.
• Do the same for both hot and cold inlet points if your model uses both.
• Reattach the hoses tightly, turn taps back on, and restart a cycle.

### 4. Check the Door Lock
While less common for a pure "water fill" error, ensure the door is fully closed and latched. If the machine doesn’t detect the door as locked, it may not start the fill process properly. Try closing it firmly again.

### 5. Reset the Machine
• Turn off the machine using the power button.
• Unplug it from the wall for 1–2 minutes.
• Plug it back in and try a new cycle. This can clear temporary electronic glitches.

### When to Call a Technician
If you’ve cleaned the filters, checked water pressure, and reset the machine but still get 4C:
• The water inlet valve itself may be faulty (electrical component failure).
• There could be an issue with the pressure sensor or main control board.

Recommendation: Start by cleaning the inlet filters – this solves ~80% of 4C errors on Samsung models and is free to do yourself.

Tap was open, and turning it fully anticlockwise made no difference. Hose isn't kinked and the kitchen cold tap pressure is normal. The water company was working in the street two days ago and our water ran brown briefly. I took the inlet hose off and the mesh filter was clogged with grey grit and limescale bits. I cleaned it, refitted it, and now it fills normally and the 4C has gone.

That is excellent news! You’ve successfully identified and resolved the root cause. The water company’s work likely stirred up sediment in the mains supply, which then traveled through your pipes and clogged the inlet filter. This is a very common issue after local water works.

Since you’ve already cleaned the filter and the machine is filling normally, here are a few quick tips to prevent this from happening again:

1.  Monitor Water Clarity: If you notice brown or discolored water coming from your taps in the future, run the cold tap for a minute before starting any appliance that uses water (washing machine, dishwasher) to flush out remaining sediment.
2.  Regular Maintenance: Check the inlet filters every 6–12 months as part of routine maintenance, especially if you have hard water or older plumbing.
3.  Consider an Inlet Filter Screen: If this happens frequently, some people install a larger external filter on the inlet hose to catch debris before it reaches the machine’s internal filters.

You’ve saved yourself a service call! Enjoy your freshly cleaned laundry.
